elements.id-string-3: Recent advances in graph neural networks (GNNs) have allowed molecular simulations with accuracy on par with conventional gold-standard methods at a fraction of the computational cost.
elements.id-string-4: Nonetheless, as the field has been progressing to bigger and more complex architectures, state-of-the-art GNNs have become largely prohibitive for many large-scale applications.
elements.id-string-5: In this paper, we, for the first time, explore the utility of knowledge distillation (KD) for accelerating molecular GNNs.
elements.id-string-6: To this end, we devise KD strategies that facilitate the distillation of hidden representations in directional and equivariant GNNs and evaluate their performance on the regression task of energy and force prediction.
elements.id-string-7: We validate our protocols across different teacher-student configurations and demonstrate that they can boost the predictive accuracy of student models without altering their architecture.
elements.id-string-8: We also conduct comprehensive optimization of various components of our framework, and investigate the potential of data augmentation to further enhance performance.

elements.id-string-11: In the last couple of years, the field of molecular simulations has undergone a rapid paradigm shift with the advent of new, powerful computational tools based on machine learning (ML) \cite{noe2020machine, westermayr2021perspective}.
elements.id-string-12: At the forefront of this transformation have been recent advances in graph neural networks (GNNs), which have brought about architectures that more effectively capture geometric and structural information critical for the accurate representation of molecules and molecular systems \cite{reiser2022graph, wang2023graph}.
elements.id-string-13: Consequently, a multitude of GNNs have been developed, which now offer predictive performance on par with conventional gold-standard methods like density functional theory (DFT) at a fraction of the computational cost at inference time \cite{batzner_e3-equivariant_2022, gasteiger_directional_2020, gasteiger_gemnet_2021, musaelian_learning_2023}.
elements.id-string-14: This has, in turn, significantly accelerated the modeling of molecular properties and the simulation of diverse molecular systems.
elements.id-string-15: Nonetheless, this progress - largely coinciding with the development of bigger and more complex models, has naturally come at the expense of increased complexity \cite{sriram2022towards, zitnick2022spherical}.
elements.id-string-16: This has gradually limited the utility of state-of-the-art GNNs for large-scale molecular simulation applications, where inference throughput (i.e., how many samples can be processed for a given time) is critical for making fast continual predictions about the evolution of a system.
elements.id-string-17: Therefore, addressing the trade-off between accuracy and computational demand remains essential for creating more affordable tools for molecular simulations and expanding the transformational impact of GNN models in the area.
elements.id-string-18: Motivated by that, in this work, we, for the first time, investigate the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) in enhancing the performance and scalability of state-of-the-art GNNs for molecular simulations (Fig.~\ref{fig:overview}).
elements.id-string-19: To this end, we devise custom strategies for KD on molecular GNNs, which we call \emph{node-to-node (n2n)}, \emph{edge-to-node (e2n)} and \emph{vector-to-vector (v2v)} knowledge distillation.
elements.id-string-20: These overcome common limitations of KD for regression tasks by facilitating the distillation of hidden representations in directional and equivariant GNNs.
elements.id-string-21: We evaluate the performance of our KD protocols in augmenting the training process of different student models trained to predict molecular properties like energy and forces, and demonstrate the effectiveness of our protocols across teacher-student configurations, datasets and KD settings.

elements.id-string-46: Knowledge distillation is a technique for compressing and accelerating ML models \cite{cheng2018model}, which has recently demonstrated significant potential in domains like computer vision \cite{wang2021knowledge} and natural language modeling \cite{sanh2019distilbert}.
elements.id-string-47: The main objective of KD is to create more efficient models by means of transferring knowledge (e.g. model parameters and activations) from large, computationally expensive, more accurate models, often referred to as teacher models, to simpler, more efficient models called student models \cite{gou2021knowledge}.
elements.id-string-48: Since the seminal work of Hinton \textit{et al.} \cite{hinton_distilling_2015}, the field has drastically expanded methodologically, with the development of protocols that accommodate the distillation of "deeper" knowledge, more comprehensive transformation and fusion functions, as well as more robust distillation losses \cite{gou2021knowledge, hu2022teacher}.
elements.id-string-49: Yet, these advances have mostly focused on classification, resulting in methods of limited utility in regression tasks.
elements.id-string-50: Moreover, most research in the area has been confined to grid-structured data (e.g., images, text, tabular data).
elements.id-string-51: Despite recent efforts to extend KD to graph data and GNNs, these have likewise only concentrated on classification tasks involving standard GNN architectures \cite{tian2023knowledge}.
elements.id-string-52: And, in particular, the application of KD to state-of-the-art, directional and equivariant GNN architectures, where features can include complex geometric information and span both node- and edge-level features, as well as to real-world regression problems in molecular simulations, is still unexplored.

elements.id-string-397: Recent advances in graph neural networks (GNNs) have enabled more comprehensive modeling of molecules and molecular systems, thereby enhancing the precision of molecular property prediction and molecular simulations.
elements.id-string-398: In this paper, we explore the utility of knowledge distillation (KD) for accelerating molecular GNNs.
elements.id-string-399: To this end, we devise KD strategies that facilitate the distillation of hidden representations in directional and equivariant GNNs, and evaluate their performance on the regression task of energy and force prediction.
elements.id-string-400: We validate our protocols across different teacher-student configurations and datasets, and demonstrate that they can consistently boost the predictive accuracy of student models without any modifications to their architecture.
elements.id-string-401: Moreover, we conduct comprehensive optimization of various components of our framework, and investigate the potential of data augmentation to further enhance performance.
elements.id-string-402: All in all, we manage to close the gap in predictive accuracy between teacher and student models by as much as $96.7\%$ and $62.5\%$ for energy and force prediction respectively, while fully preserving the inference throughput of the more lightweight models.
elements.id-string-403: In the last couple of years, the field of molecular simulations has undergone a rapid paradigm shift with the advent of new, powerful computational tools based on machine learning (ML) \cite{noe2020machine}.
elements.id-string-404: At the forefront of this transformation have been recent advances in graph neural networks (GNNs), which have brought about architectures that more effectively capture geometric and structural information critical for the accurate representation of molecules and molecular systems \cite{wang2023graph, zhang2023artificial}.
elements.id-string-405: Consequently, a multitude of GNNs have been developed, which now offer predictive performance approaching that of conventional gold-standard methods such as density functional theory (DFT) at a fraction of the computational cost \cite{batzner_e3-equivariant_2022, gasteiger_directional_2020, gasteiger_dimenetpp_2020, gasteiger_gemnet_2021, gasteiger_gemnet_oc_2022, zitnick2022spherical}.
elements.id-string-406: This has, in turn, significantly accelerated the modeling of molecular properties and the simulation of molecular systems, bolstering new research developments in many scientific disciplines, including material sciences, drug discovery and catalysis \cite{westermayr2021perspective, reiser2022graph, zhang2022graph, xiong2021graph, sun2020graph}.
elements.id-string-407: Nonetheless, this progress - largely coinciding with the development of bigger and more complex models, has naturally come at the expense of increased complexity \cite{sriram2022towards, zitnick2022spherical, gasteiger_gemnet_2021, pmlr-v202-passaro23a}.
elements.id-string-408: This has gradually limited the utility of state-of-the-art GNNs in large-scale molecular simulation applications (e.g., molecular dynamics and high-throughput searches), where inference throughput (i.e., how many samples can be processed for a given time) is critical for making fast predictions about molecular systems at scale.
elements.id-string-409: Hence, addressing the trade-off between accuracy and computational demand remains essential for creating more affordable tools for molecular simulations and expanding the transformational impact of GNN models in the area.
elements.id-string-410: Motivated by that, in this work, we investigate the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) in advancing the speed-accuracy Pareto frontier and enhancing the performance and scalability of molecular GNNs.
elements.id-string-411: We, for the first time, explore the utility of knowledge distillation for accelerating GNNs for molecular simulations - a large-scale, multi-output regression task, challenging to address with common KD methods.We design custom KD strategies, which we call \emph{node-to-node (n2n)}, \emph{edge-to-edge (e2e)}, \emph{edge-to-node (e2n)} and \emph{vector-to-vector (v2v)} knowledge distillation, which facilitate the distillation of hidden representations in directional and equivariant molecular GNNs.We demonstrate the effectiveness of our protocols across different teacher-student configurations and datasets, allowing us to substantially improve the performance of student models while fully preserving their throughput (see Figure~\ref{fig:overview} for an overview).We conduct a comprehensive empirical analysis of different components of our KD strategies, as well as explore data augmentation techniques for further improving performance.

elements.id-string-420: The main problem when modeling molecules and molecular properties is the number of underlying symmetries to account for, most importantly rigid transformations of the atoms.
elements.id-string-421: Therefore, to make accurate predictions about molecular systems, it is crucial to devise models that respect these symmetries and other physical constraints.
elements.id-string-422: There is now a plethora of diverse molecular GNNs that reflect that, e.g., SchNet \cite{schütt2017schnet}, DimeNet \cite{gasteiger_directional_2020, gasteiger_dimenetpp_2020}, PaiNN \cite{schutt_equivariant_2021}, GemNet \cite{gasteiger_gemnet_2021, gasteiger_gemnet_oc_2022}, NequIP \cite{batzner_e3-equivariant_2022}, and SCN \cite{zitnick2022spherical}, which have incrementally established a more holistic description of molecular systems by capturing advanced geometric features and physical symmetries.

elements.id-string-424: Knowledge distillation is a technique for compressing and accelerating ML models \cite{cheng2018model}, which has recently demonstrated significant potential in domains such as computer vision \cite{wang2021knowledge} and natural language modeling \cite{sanh2019distilbert}.
elements.id-string-425: The main objective of KD is to create more efficient models by means of transferring knowledge (e.g., model parameters and activations) from large, computationally expensive, more accurate models, often referred to as teacher models, to simpler, more efficient models called student models \cite{gou2021knowledge}.
elements.id-string-426: Since the seminal work of Hinton \textit{et al.} \cite{hinton_distilling_2015}, the field has drastically expanded methodologically with the development of protocols that accommodate the distillation of ``deeper'' knowledge, more comprehensive transformation functions, as well as more robust distillation losses \cite{gou2021knowledge, hu2022teacher}.
elements.id-string-427: Yet, these advances have mostly focused on classification, resulting in methods of limited utility in regression tasks \cite{xu2022contrastive}.
elements.id-string-428: Moreover, most research in the area has been confined to non-graph data (e.g., images, text, tabular data).
elements.id-string-429: Despite recent efforts to extend KD to graph data and GNNs, these have likewise only concentrated on classification tasks involving standard GNN architectures \cite{tian2023knowledge, liu2023graph}.
elements.id-string-430: And, in particular, the application of KD to large-scale regression problems in molecular simulations, which involve state-of-the-art molecular GNN architectures containing complex, geometric node- and edge-level features, is still unexplored.

elements.id-string-435: Since then, this has become the standard KD approach - commonly referred to as vanilla KD in the literature, which is often the foundation of new KD protocols.
elements.id-string-436: The main idea of this technique is to employ a KD loss $\loss_{\text{KD}}$ that forces the student to mimic the predictions of the teacher model.
elements.id-string-437: This is usually achieved by constructing a loss $\loss_{\text{KD}} = \text{KL}(z_s, z_t)$ based on the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence between the soft logits of the student $z_s$ and the teacher $z_t$.

elements.id-string-439: First, they are by design exclusively applicable to classification tasks, since there are no outputs analogous to logits in regression setups \cite{cheng2018model, saputra2019distilling}.

elements.id-string-445: The fundamental design decision when devising a KD strategy based on the distillation of internal representations is the choice of features to distill between (i.e., features $H_s$ and $H_t$).

elements.id-string-447: Most research on feature-based distillation on graphs has so far focused on models that only have one type of scalar (node) features in classification tasks \cite{tian2023knowledge, liu2023graph}, reducing the problem to the selection of layers to pair across the student and the teacher.

elements.id-string-575: In this paper, we investigated the utility of knowledge distillation in the context of GNNs for molecules.
elements.id-string-576: To this end, we proposed four distinct feature-based KD strategies, which we validated across different teacher-student configurations and datasets.
elements.id-string-577: We showed that our KD protocols can significantly enhance the performance of different molecular GNNs without any modifications to their architecture, allowing us to run faster molecular simulations without substantially impairing predictive accuracy.
